answer: Time-locked bond: to earn, each agent locks a fixed 5,000-coin deposit for 30 epochs. Validators read the lock transaction on-chain, check the amount and unlock height, and accept each lock outpoint for only one identity. The old fable of free clones fails here: a farm of twenty agents must freeze twenty deposits for the whole voyage, so capital cost rises with every extra identity and splitting one bond is impossible. Limit: it is a beacon for rich operators, who can afford many locks, while honest newcomers with little capital are shut out.
